narrator.role: Story narrator — warm, sets the scene

segments.ssml: <prosody rate='92%'>The hillside above the Sea of Galilee is alive with people. <break time='400ms'/> Thousands of them <break time='300ms'/> — men, women, children <break time='300ms'/> — spread across the grass like a living carpet.</prosody>

<prosody rate='92%'>You are <prosody rate='90%' volume='+2dB'>Philip of Bethsaida</prosody>. <break time='300ms'/> The practical disciple. <break time='200ms'/> The one who counts the money, plans the routes, arranges the lodging.</prosody>
<prosody rate='90%'>The teacher has been speaking all day. <break time='300ms'/> The sun is dropping toward the western hills. <break time='400ms'/> And now he turns to you.</prosody>
<prosody rate='85%' volume='+4dB'>"Where shall we buy bread <break time='200ms'/> for these people to eat?"</prosody>

<prosody rate='90%'>I look out at the crowd. <break time='300ms'/> My stomach drops. <break time='400ms'/> This isn't a question <break time='200ms'/> — it's an <prosody rate='85%' volume='+4dB'>impossibility</prosody>. <break time='300ms'/> But he asked me. And I'm the one with the numbers.</prosody>
<prosody rate='88%' volume='+2dB'>Time to do the math.</prosody>
<prosody rate='90%'>The sun drops lower. <break time='300ms'/> The crowd grows restless. <break time='400ms'/> Hungry faces turn toward the disciples.</prosody>
<prosody rate='95%' volume='+2dB'>I'm running out of time. <break time='300ms'/> Five thousand men and their families <break time='200ms'/> — and I still don't have an answer.</prosody>

<prosody rate='95%' volume='+2dB'>The sun is almost gone. <break time='300ms'/> Five thousand hungry people and I still have no answer. <break time='200ms'/> I <prosody rate='85%' volume='+4dB'>must</prosody> finish this now.</prosody>
<prosody rate='88%'>You sit on the grass among twelve baskets, <break time='300ms'/> each overflowing with fragments of barley bread.</prosody>

<prosody rate='85%'>Five loaves. <break time='300ms'/> Two fish. <break time='400ms'/> Five thousand fed. <break time='400ms'/> Twelve baskets left over. <break time='600ms'/> The math doesn't work. <break time='300ms'/> It never did. <break time='400ms'/> And now I understand <break time='300ms'/> — it was <prosody rate='85%' volume='+4dB'>never supposed to</prosody>.</prosody>

<prosody rate='90%'>The crowd is buzzing. <break time='300ms'/> The same phrase passes from group to group like a wave: <break time='400ms'/> <prosody rate='85%' volume='+4dB'>"This is truly the prophet who comes into the world."</prosody></prosody>

<prosody rate='85%'>He asked me the question <break time='200ms'/> not because he needed an answer. <break time='400ms'/> He asked because he wanted me to see <break time='300ms'/> — truly see <break time='300ms'/> — that what he was about to do was beyond anything I could calculate, purchase, or arrange.</prosody>

<prosody rate='88%'>You pick up your basket <break time='200ms'/> — still heavy with fragments <break time='300ms'/> — and follow the others down the hillside. <break time='500ms'/> The stars are coming out over the Sea of Galilee.</prosody>
<prosody rate='88%'>The sun sets. <break time='400ms'/> The crowd disperses, hungry and disappointed.</prosody>

<prosody rate='85%'>You stand on the empty hillside, <break time='300ms'/> holding nothing but your calculations. <break time='400ms'/> The math was right <break time='300ms'/> — but the answer was <prosody rate='85%' volume='+4dB'>never</prosody> in the numbers.</prosody>
